source.title: Generative Audio Language Modeling with Continuous-valued Tokens and Masked Next-Token Prediction
source.authors: Shu-Wen Yang; Byeonggeun Kim; Kuan-Po Huang; Qingming Tang; Huy Phan; Bo-Ru Lu; Harshavardhan Sundar; Shalini Ghosh; Hung-Yi Lee; Chieh-Chi Kao; Chao Wang

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper and appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares two model sizes for audio generation and reports how evaluation metrics change, extending scale-related evaluation to audio. It does not measure held-out loss or test a power law.
record.gate_note: The paper cites language-model scaling laws in its introduction, but does not test them. It reports a two-size AudioMNTP comparison on audio-generation quality metrics. These results do not test power-law loss, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or downstream-task predictability. Other model comparisons and MNTP ablations are not rows for the scaling claim.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes an audio generation method (AudioMNTP). It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only as background. Its one size comparison is two models (193M vs 462M), and that comparison also changes the diffusion head (3 vs 6 MLP layers). The outcomes are generation-quality metrics, not held-out loss. No power law is fitted, extrapolated or checked for allocation. The record's 'tests'/T3 is wrong: no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors' main conclusions are that continuous-valued tokens and masked next-token prediction (MNTP) give SOTA-level causal audio generation. On scale, they say scaling to Large improves most metrics and that further scaling could help. They make no power-law claim.
record.recipe_differences: Uses two audio-generation model sizes and AudioCaps quality metrics; does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy, fit scaling laws, or vary compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported changes differ by metric: most improve from AudioMNTP Base to Large, while KL changes from 1.16 to 1.17.

fits_no_version.finding: Going from AudioMNTP Base (193M, 3-layer head) to Large (462M, 6-layer head) improves FD, FAD, IS and CLAP; KL is flat (1.16 to 1.17).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger continuous-token audio LMs give better text-to-audio generation quality (two sizes only, confounded by head size).

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The size comparison has only two model sizes, and the reported outcomes are audio-generation metrics rather than held-out pretraining loss. No scaling-law fit, uncertainty estimate for the objective metrics, or compute-budget sweep is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Other benchmark-model comparisons in Table 1 and model/task ablations in Tables 3–8 are not included because they do not report the effect of model-size scaling on the claim's named measures.

untested.parts: No loss sweep over parameters, tokens or compute.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
The study is in audio, but it fits no power law, so whether the form holds in audio is untested.
No predictability analysis; only two sizes on quality metrics.
No comparison of fits or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation and tranche guesses (tests/T3) are overruled to cites_only/T6, consistent with the record's own gate_note. Appendix F.2 shows the Large model also uses a 6-layer head versus 3 for Base. Table 4 shows the head change alone produces a similar FAD gain, so the size comparison is confounded.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run power-law fits or predictions of much larger runs.
No fixed-compute-budget allocation sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token scaling.
No controlled comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study is in audio, but does not test whether a power-law form holds in audio or other modalities or training regimes.
It reports audio-generation evaluation metrics at two sizes, not downstream-task performance predictability or a relation to pretraining loss.
No comparison of scaling-law fits, exponents, or fitting choices.

rows.subject: AudioMNTP Large
rows.stage_stated: Fine-tuned from pre-trained image MAR on audio data
rows.operation_detail: Compared the 462M AudioMNTP Large model with the 193M AudioMNTP Base model.
rows.note: One of five reported evaluation metrics in the two-size comparison; no power-law fit is reported.
rows.check: Two-point size comparison on FD; the diffusion head is also changed (3 vs 6 MLP layers). Cannot bear on any power-law version.

rows.stage_stated: Fine-tuned from pre-trained image MAR on audio data
rows.operation_detail: Compared the 462M AudioMNTP Large model with the 193M AudioMNTP Base model.
rows.note: The authors describe this as a 27% relative improvement over AudioMNTP Base.
rows.check: Two-point size comparison on FAD. It is confounded by head size: Table 4 shows the 6-layer head alone cuts Base FAD 1.68 to 1.21.
